place_name: Crystal Lake Wall, Lake George, Mammoth Lakes Area, Eastern Sierra, CA
approach_stated: 40-50 minutes from the Lake George parking area via Crystal Lake Trail (~1 mi to junction, then use trail)
summit_or_glacier: no; 12-25 m single-pitch granite crag at 9,700 ft

evidence.fact: Pleasant granite crag, sport/mixed/trad routes 12-25m, 9700ft; from Lake George parking hike Crystal Lake Trail; approach 40-50 minutes.

note: MP route types also carry an Alpine flag (e.g. 'Sport, Alpine'); routes 15-23 m single pitch.

place_name: Black Bluff - N. Face (Left Side), Mill Creek Rd/Skyline Drive Area, Big Bear South, San Bernardino Mtns, CA
approach_stated: About 1.5 miles from parking before Bluff Mesa Group Campground, across the mesa (no time stated)
summit_or_glacier: no; 80 ft granite cliff on the edge of a mesa

evidence.fact: Remote crag on the mesa edge west of Bluff Mesa Group Camp; granite about 80 ft; approach about 1.5 miles via cairns.
Smaller, blockier side of north face; handful of gear routes 5.8-5.11c; follow trail downhill to the base.

note: Only a distance (1.5 mi, flat mesa) is stated, not a time. All four routes MP 'Trad, Alpine', 80 ft. Area had a temporary Line Fire closure notice.

place_name: The Rectory - East Face, Church Domes, Domeland Wilderness, Southern Sierra, CA
approach_stated: Church Domes: about 30 minutes hiking from the logging road, well-cairned
summit_or_glacier: no glacier; single-pitch 70-100 ft routes on a dome face, no summit finish stated

evidence.fact: From the logging road, the Domes are about 30 minutes' hiking, well-cairned; road may be impassable after first big snow.
East face across a steep notch from the Convent, a number of bolted lines in the .10s; routes 70-100 ft.

note: MP types 'Trad, Alpine' for all; Domeland Wilderness; dirt road access, high-clearance can drive one more mile.

place_name: Merriam Peak, Royce Lakes, Humphreys Basin area, High Sierra, CA
approach_stated: Pine Creek trailhead, past Pine Lake, Upper Pine Lake and Honeymoon Lake, cross-country over Royce Pass (11,680 ft) to Royce Lakes (no total time stated)
summit_or_glacier: 13,077 ft High Sierra peak; backcountry cirque setting

evidence.fact: Pine Creek trailhead, up to Pine Lake and Honeymoon Lake, then cross-country over Royce Pass (11,680ft) to Royce Lakes.

note: Roadless backcountry approach over an 11,680 ft pass. MP types carry Alpine flag.

place_name: Siberia Creek Tower - South Face, Siberia Creek, Mill Creek Rd/Skyline Drive Area, Big Bear South, CA
approach_stated: Follow Siberia Creek from trailhead parking about a mile (boardwalk creek crossings), then scramble a boulder gully to the south face (no time stated)
summit_or_glacier: no; tower crag with single-pitch trad, TR and sport routes, 7,422 ft

evidence.fact: Follow Siberia Creek from trailhead parking about a mile; the second formation on the right is Siberia Creek Tower.
At least 14 gear climbs and 9 sport routes, mostly on the sunny south side.

note: Only a distance (~1 mile) is stated, not a time. MP types carry the Alpine flag.

place_name: Arctic Temple, Mill Creek Rd/Skyline Drive Area, Big Bear South, San Bernardino Mtns, CA
approach_stated: Approach: 20-40 minutes
summit_or_glacier: no glacier; descent is a downclimb off the formation top (crag formation, 7,400 ft)

evidence.fact: Approach: 20-40 minutes. Descent: downclimb. One of the largest formations in the San Bernardinos; stellar 5.10 trad.

note: MP types Trad, Alpine.

place_name: Main Wall, Tiger Cliff, Timberline Lake area, Leadville, CO
approach_stated: Tiger Cliff approach is 1.5 hours ('on the long side for a single-pitch crag')
summit_or_glacier: no summit/glacier; single-pitch ~30 m routes at 12,000 ft

evidence.fact: While the approach is on the long side (1.5 hours) for a single-pitch crag, the excellent routes make it worth the effort.
Longest section of Tiger Cliff, east-facing; all routes very close to 30m; walk up the grassy slope from the meadow.

note: Alpine only by the >60-min approach rule; MP itself calls it a single-pitch crag. MP types Trad, Alpine.

place_name: Chasm View Wall, Long's Peak, Rocky Mountain NP, CO
approach_stated: Long's Peak trailhead to Chasm Lake 4.5 mi, then scree/boulders to the base; MP Long's Peak page: approach at least 5 miles
summit_or_glacier: 13,000 ft wall on Longs Peak, 4-7 pitch routes ending near Boulder Field / Chasm View rappels

evidence.fact: Hike up to Chasm Lake, 4.5 mi; ascend scree/boulders to the base. Nearly 20 routes 4-7 pitches.
Highest peak in RMNP; this approach will be at least 5 miles.

note: MP types Trad, Alpine.

place_name: Chicago Creek Rock, Mt. Blue Sky (Mt. Evans) Road / CO 103, CO
approach_stated: none in minutes; crag is 'within sight of Colo 103'
summit_or_glacier: no; south-facing granite crag, routes 70-190 ft

evidence.fact: One of the better crags along Chicago Creek on CO 103; mountain setting, although within sight of Colo 103.

note: Almost certainly a roadside crag but no approach time/distance stated on MP. MP types carry Alpine flag. PTSD is 2 pitches.

place_name: West Face, Long's Peak, Rocky Mountain NP, CO
approach_stated: Long's Peak Trail to the Boulderfield, through the Keyhole, then scramble; MP Long's Peak page: approach at least 5 miles
summit_or_glacier: 14er summit-block face (~14,000 ft), reached via the Keyhole

evidence.fact: From Long's Peak Trailhead hike to the Boulderfield, continue through the Keyhole, turn south; West Face on your left.
Highest peak in RMNP; this approach will be at least 5 miles.

note: MP types Trad, Alpine.

place_name: McHenry's Peak, Glacier Gorge, Rocky Mountain NP, CO
approach_stated: Glacier Gorge Trail to Black Lake, then northwest from the shelf above Black Lake (no time stated; Shelf Lake path branches after about 4 miles)
summit_or_glacier: 13,327 ft peak; multi-pitch faces/ridges (Pair of Jacks 6 pitches)

evidence.fact: Massive peak forming the northern shoulder of Glacier Gorge; head northwest from the shelf above Black Lake.
Glacier Gorge Trail past Mills and Jewel Lakes to Black Lake, then cairns into the upper cirque.

note: MP types Trad, Alpine.

place_name: Shoshoni Peak, Indian Peaks, CO
approach_stated: not stated in time; buttresses above the Isabelle Glacier trail, descent walks off the back to the Pawnee Pass Trail
summit_or_glacier: glacier setting (southern ramparts loom over Isabelle Glacier); 12,952 ft peak, ridge traversing to escape

evidence.fact: Southern ramparts loom over the Isabelle Glacier; twin 500-foot buttresses above the Isabelle Glacier trail; descend to Pawnee Pass Trail.

note: co_unknown_5 (Unknown 5.9) not matched to a specific MP route id; MP lists an 'Unknown' route here. Finnacle Ridge is 6 pitches.

place_name: The Lair, Empire (Ra area, 3.2 mi N of Empire on the road), CO
approach_stated: Roadside parking 3.2 mi north of Empire; The Lair is 'just across the tailings field', bolts visible from the trail (no minutes stated)
summit_or_glacier: no; cave crag low on the hillside, routes 60-90 ft

evidence.fact: Cave-like feature east of Ra, low on the hillside, just across the tailings field; bolts on two routes visible from the trail.
Ra is 3.2 miles north of the light in Empire at 9000 ft; parking on both sides of the road.

note: No approach minutes stated; verdict rests on 'just across the tailings field' from road parking. All MP types carry Alpine flag.

place_name: Petit Grepon, Sky Pond, Loch Vale, Rocky Mountain NP, CO
approach_stated: About 5 miles from Glacier Gorge trailhead to Sky Pond; ~2 hours trailhead to base
summit_or_glacier: summit finish (routes end on the spire summit, 6 rappels); multipitch Grade III

evidence.fact: Park at Glacier Gorge Junction Trailhead and hike five miles or so to Sky Pond; summit one of the most spectacular in the Park.
Glacier Gorge Trailhead to base of route: 2 hours; continue to the ridge and go to the summit.

note: MP types 'Trad, Alpine', 6-8 pitches Grade III.

place_name: Rip Rap, Wild Ridge Area, Independence Pass, CO
approach_stated: About 30 minutes from the Wild Rock pullout on CO 82 to the base of Wild Ridge
summit_or_glacier: no; finishing band above The Wave, reached by climbing routes through The Wave

evidence.fact: Park as for Wild Rock on CO 82; cairned traverse and talus to the base of the wall. This takes about 30 minutes.
Standard approach is to climb routes through The Wave and set up for a finishing pitch through the Rip Rap.

note: Options are 30-80 ft finishing pitches atop Wild Ridge (~10,700 ft). MP types carry Alpine flag.

place_name: The Saber, Sky Pond, Loch Vale, Rocky Mountain NP, CO
approach_stated: Trail to Sky Pond ~3.5 mi (MP notes closer to 5 mi) then talus; ~2 hours trailhead to base
summit_or_glacier: spire; SW Corner ends on a subsummit above a notch; 5-10 pitch Grade III, 11,856 ft

evidence.fact: From Glacier Gorge parking head up the trail to Sky Pond (about 3 1/2 miles, actually closer to 5) and scramble talus to base.
Glacier Gorge Trailhead to base of route: 2 hours; route ends on a little summit above a notch.

note: MP types 'Trad, Alpine'.

place_name: Keyboard of the Winds, SW ridge of Longs Peak, Rocky Mountain NP, CO
approach_stated: From Glacier Gorge past Black Lake, 5 mi, to Green Lake, then up toward the Pagoda-Longs col
summit_or_glacier: ridge towers at 13,600 ft on Longs Peak SW ridge

evidence.fact: Along SW ridge of Long's Peak connecting with Pagoda; approach from Glacier Gorge past Black Lake, 5mi, to Green Lake, then up to col.

note: MP types 'Trad, Alpine'; elevation 13,600 ft.

place_name: The Portal, Pass Creek Canyon, Lost River Range, Central Idaho
approach_stated: Climbing never more than 100 m from Pass Creek (gravel road through the canyon); Portal is just around the corner from the large natural cave via an obvious trail
summit_or_glacier: no; short bolted sport routes on a grassy ledge, 6,486 ft

evidence.fact: Climbing is never more than one hundred meters from Pass Creek; well-maintained gravel road bisects the range.
Highest sector in canyon; short routes, all bolted to sport anchors; just around the corner from the large natural cave.

note: MP types Sport (no Alpine flag) for all four.

place_name: Harrison Peak, Selkirk Crest (American), North Idaho
approach_stated: Pack River Road nearly to its end, hike to Harrison Lake, then cross-country up talus and 3rd/4th class slabs (no time stated)
summit_or_glacier: summit: 'multipitch rock routes to its summit' (7,292 ft)

evidence.fact: Impressive Selkirk peak with multipitch rock routes to its summit; hike to Harrison Lake, then cross-country up talus and slabs.

note: MP types Trad, Alpine; Running Flakes 3 pitches.

place_name: Upper Science Friction, Nova Canyon, Sandia Mountains, Albuquerque Area, NM
approach_stated: ~25 minutes from the Sandia Crest parking lot (downhill), first area reached in Nova Canyon
summit_or_glacier: no; single/multi-pitch crag walls below the crest

evidence.fact: Approach time: ~25 minutes from the Sandia Crest parking lot to climber's right side of Upper Science Friction.
One of the first areas you arrive at in Nova Canyon; once 'hidden', now much more accessible.

note: Approach descends from the crest, so the return is uphill. 1993: A Face Odyssey is 2 pitches. MP types Trad (no Alpine flag).

place_name: Donald Duck, La Cueva Canyon (Upper), Sandia Mountains, NM
approach_stated: Approach time is around 30 minutes (down La Luz trail from the Crest, past The Fin)
summit_or_glacier: short tower top (rappel anchor off the formation); no mountain summit or glacier

evidence.fact: Short tower south of the La Luz trail just above The Fin; hike down La Luz from the Crest. Approach time is around 30 minutes.

note: Approach descends from the Crest, so the return is uphill. MP types have no Alpine flag.

place_name: Mt Owen, Grand Teton NP, WY
approach_stated: Not stated in time; common approaches via Teton Glacier / Surprise Lake to the Koven Couloir and East Ridge
summit_or_glacier: summit (12,928 ft, no route easier than 5th class) and glacier/snow approaches

evidence.fact: Second highest peak in the range, no route easier than 5th class to its summit; common ascent is Koven couloir from Teton Glacier.

note: All MP types carry Alpine flag; several also Snow. Serendipity Arete type read from MP search result row.

place_name: Punk Rock - Right Side of East Face, Courtright Reservoir, Hwy 168, Southern Sierra West Slope, CA
approach_stated: Punk Rock dome visible from the Maxon parking lot, closest climbs about 5 minutes from the car; this sector is reached shortly after the talus traverse used for the 64th Birthday area
summit_or_glacier: no; low-angle face, routes to bolt anchors at 35 m

evidence.fact: From the Maxon parking lot you will see the dome on your right. The closest climbs are about 5 minutes from the car.
Low-angle face, three routes to bolt anchors at 35 m; same approach as 64th Birthday area, shortly after the talus traverse.

note: Exact minutes to this sector not stated; it is past the 5-min closest climbs. MP types Trad (no Alpine flag).

place_name: Probably Tiger Cage, Courtright Reservoir, Hwy 168, Southern Sierra West Slope, CA (no 'Upper Tier' found on MP)
approach_stated: Tiger Cage (Courtright): 'easily accessed from the main road' via a faint use trail from a pullout before the Y / Marmot Rock Campground (no time stated)
summit_or_glacier: no (Tiger Cage is a 5.7-5.10 crack crag at 5,070 ft)

evidence.fact: Tiger Cage: steep cracks 5.7-5.10; easily accessed from the main road via a faint use trail.

note: Could not match: MP Tiger Cage has no 'Upper Tier' sub-area and no routes named 'Unknown 5.7/5.8/5.10a/5.10c'. Identity unconfirmed, so no route types recorded.

place_name: Quandary Peak (Blue Lakes / McCullough Gulch buttresses), Tenmile Range, CO
approach_stated: Snowblind: about 5 minutes from Blue Lakes; Golden Goat Buttress: a short hike above the lower lake parking; King's Crown: cliffs between lower and upper McCullough Gulch lakes (no time)
summit_or_glacier: no summit for the sample routes (1-2 pitch buttresses, scramble/couloir descent); the peak itself is a 14er

evidence.fact: At Blue Lakes, follow the trail on the right side of the lake for about 5 minutes to an obvious slab.
Park at the lower lake lot; Golden Goat Buttress is just a short hike above the parking area; 2 pitches.

note: Area also holds true alpine lines (Inwood Arete, Cristo Couloir) not in this sample. King's Crown approach time unstated (McCullough Gulch). All MP types carry the Alpine flag.

place_name: Main Wall, Cedar Creek, Lost River Range, Central Idaho
approach_stated: One hour hike from the end of the road
summit_or_glacier: no; steep single-pitch sport wall along Cedar Creek, 8,553 ft

evidence.fact: All-day shade along Cedar Creek; longest, steepest routes at Cedar Creek. Getting There: One hour hike from the end of the road.

note: Exactly at the 60-min line. MP types Sport, Alpine.

place_name: The Tree House, Wolverine Bowl, Bridger Range, Bozeman Area, MT
approach_stated: 1 hour hike from parking to Wolverine Bowl (45 min if quick), then past the Bud Wall and over a saddle to the Tree House
summit_or_glacier: no summit/glacier; single-pitch sport wall at 7,796 ft

evidence.fact: From the parking lot it is a 1 hour hike to Wolverine (45min if hiking quickly).
From where the Bud Wall trail fizzles, cross to the saddle and descend to the Tree House; outside the main bowl.

note: Borderline: stated time to the bowl is 45-60 min and the Tree House lies beyond it, so the total exceeds 60 min. Sport routes with MP Alpine flag; no summit.

place_name: Beehive Peak, Beehive Basin, Spanish Peaks Wilderness, Big Sky Area, MT
approach_stated: 4 mile hike to the basin, then about 1.5 more miles to the summit
summit_or_glacier: summit peak at 10,246 ft (wilderness cirque)

evidence.fact: It is a 4 mile hike to the basin, which provides nice camping (Wilderness), and another 1.5 miles to the summit.
Moderate approach compared to most alpine settings; trail to a lake at the base of the cirque, continue to the peak.

note: MP types Trad, Alpine.

place_name: Ben Wall (Crawford Crack Crag), Mt Willard, Crawford Notch, NH
approach_stated: Probably no further than 75 ft from Rt 302; about 2 minutes' walk from Hattie's parking
summit_or_glacier: no; true roadside crag, 35-40 ft routes

evidence.fact: Probably no further than 75 ft from Rt 302, this true roadside crag provides several short (35-40 ft) steep routes.

note: MP types Trad, Alpine (Alpine flag despite roadside).

place_name: Willey Brook Ravine, Mt Willard, Crawford Notch, NH
approach_stated: From Hattie's Garden walk to the big bridge, then climbers' trail 2 min to the crag
summit_or_glacier: no; small ravine crag at 2,008 ft

evidence.fact: From Hattie's Garden walk to the big bridge and cut right into the woods. Follow the climbers trail for 2 min to the crag.

note: MP types carry the Alpine flag.
